name: Loire Valley

known.via: English Wikipedia "Loire Valley wine" (redirects to "Loire Valley (wine)")

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

keyfacts: The Upper Loire has Sauvignon Blanc in Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé, and the Lower Loire reaches the Atlantic through Muscadet, where Melon dominates.
The Middle Loire, around Touraine, Saumur, Chinon and Vouvray, is dominated by Chenin Blanc and Cabernet Franc.
Most production is white wine from Chenin Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc and Melon, with red wines from Cabernet Franc, especially around Chinon.
Because of the marginal climate, vintage quality has a bigger effect on Loire wines than on those of other French wine regions.
With Crémant production throughout the Loire, it is the second largest sparkling wine producer in France after Champagne.

blurb.text: The wine regions along the Loire river, from Muscadet on the Atlantic coast to Sancerre in the east.
